primary_outcome_name: Muscle thickness (hypertrophy) of the quadriceps femoris (rectus femoris and vastus lateralis, measured at 30/50/70% femur length) and triceps surae (medial/lateral gastrocnemius, soleus), assessed by B-mode ultrasound. This is the first-named outcome domain in the Abstract ('Muscle growth outcomes included assessments of muscle thickness...'); the paper never uses the word 'primary' or 'co-primary' anywhere in the text, and treats 9 muscle-thickness/body-composition sites as statistically co-equal (Table 2). Rectus femoris 50% (registry outcome_var) is one of these 9 sites.
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: Muscle thickness in mm, B-mode ultrasound imaging (Model E1, SonoScape), continuous, no fixed scale min/max
primary_timepoint: Post-intervention (end of 9-week training block, ultrasound taken >=48h after the last training session) vs. baseline (Pre); single pre-post comparison, no intermediate muscle-thickness timepoint
contrast_reported_primary: DELOAD vs TRAD (Group Difference = DELOAD minus TRAD; positive values favour inclusion of the deload/detraining period, negative values favour TRAD/control, per Fig. 2 caption)
population_detail: 39 resistance-trained young men (n=29) and women (n=10) completing the study (50 randomised), university population, aged 18-40 years, resistance-trained >=1 year (>=3 sessions/week), free of cardiorespiratory/musculoskeletal disorders and anabolic steroid use.

published_estimate.quote: Rectus femoris 50% (mm) ... Univariate Group Difference [95%CrI]: -0.63 [-2.8 to 1.5] ... Posterior probability favoring inclusion of detraining: p = 0.273. (Multivariate Group Difference [95%CrI]: -0.33 [-2.0 to 1.4], p = 0.347.) [Table 2, p. 11]. Note: the tabulated 'p' is a Bayesian posterior probability that the group difference favours inclusion of a deload period, not a frequentist two-sided p-value; the paper states inferences are based on 'estimates of the difference in change between DELOAD and TRAD and their credible intervals' (Statistical analyses, p. 8).

B_covariate_list: None. The Statistical analyses section describes only group (DELOAD vs TRAD) and time as model terms ('The effects of group... were estimated using univariate and multivariate multilevel regression models'); no covariate (e.g., sex, age, baseline) is stated as an adjustment term for the primary group-difference estimate. SEX is reported only as a descriptive baseline characteristic (count of men/women per group), not as a modelled covariate.
registration_id: OSF preregistration https://osf.io/bztka (methods preregistered prior to recruitment); data/materials at https://osf.io/kdgv3 (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/KDGV3)
data_availability_statement: The data and supplementary material are available at Open Science Framework: Schoenfeld, Brad J. 2023. "The Effects of a One-Week Deload Period during Regimented Resistance Training on Muscular Adaptations." OSF. December 21. doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/KDGV3.

registry_check.issues: 1) No declared primary outcome: the word 'primary' (or 'co-primary') does not occur anywhere in the paper. The registry note 'Muskeldicke koprimaer an mehreren Stellen' is a reasonable inference from the symmetric treatment of 9 muscle-thickness/body-composition outcomes in Table 2, but is not the authors' own language. RF50 (Rectus femoris 50%) is one of these 9 co-equal sites; it is somewhat more prominent than RF30/RF70/VL30/VL70/lateral gastrocnemius/soleus because it is one of only 3 sites (RF50, VL50, medial gastrocnemius) entered into the multivariate composite model, but the paper never singles it out as THE primary outcome. 2) arm_control mismatch: registry.csv codes arm_control='1', but checking the raw deposited dataset (Dataset Deload.xlsx, GROUP column) against Table 1 descriptive stats shows GROUP=1 has n=18 with RF50 Pre/Post means 41.4/45.5 mm, which matches the DELOAD arm (n=18) in Table 1 -- i.e. GROUP=1 is DELOAD, the intervention/experimental arm, not the control. GROUP=2 (n=21, RF50 Pre/Post 44.7/49.3 mm) matches TRAD (n=21), which the paper itself treats as the de facto control/reference arm (Fig. 2/3 captions: 'Negative values favor control and positive values favor the inclusion of a detraining period'; Limitations: 'the TRAD condition (which essentially served as a control)'). So the registry's arm_control value ('1') is coded to the wrong group; the true control arm is GROUP=2 (TRAD). 3) covars_published=SEX in registry does not match the paper: the Statistical analyses section lists no covariates (only 'group' and repeated-measures/time terms) for the primary group-difference models; sex is reported only descriptively, not as an adjustment covariate.

analysis_method_quote: All analyses were conducted in R (version 4.2.0) ... within a Bayesian framework, with descriptive values expressed in means +/- SDs. ... Inferences were not drawn on baseline nor within-group change, as baseline testing is inconsequential (Senn, 1994) and within-group outcomes are not the subject of our research question (Bland & Altman, 2011)... The effects of group (DELOAD vs. TRAD) on outcome variables were estimated using univariate and multivariate multilevel regression models (Vickerstaff, Ambler & Omar, 2021). Use of multivariate models improves precision by modeling all outcome variables simultaneously... Additionally, the multilevel component of the analysis accounted for the repeated measures made on each participant across outcomes and time points. ... Inferences were made based on estimates of the difference in change between DELOAD and TRAD and their credible intervals. [Statistical analyses, p. 8]
notes: Both the sonographer and the statistician were blinded to group allocation (Blinding, p. 8). The published inferential framework is fully Bayesian (brms/Stan); tables report posterior median group differences with 95% credible intervals and a 'posterior probability favoring inclusion of detraining' (not a classical p-value) -- treat any downstream comparison against frequentist alpha thresholds with care. No multiplicity adjustment across the many outcomes is reported or apparently intended, consistent with the Bayesian framing. Randomisation was block randomisation (2 participants/block) via randomizer.org, not explicitly stratified. Of 50 randomised, 39 completed and were analysed (18 DELOAD, 21 TRAD); dropouts (n=11: personal reasons n=5, non-compliance n=5, injury n=1) were excluded outright (CONSORT: 'Excluded from analysis (n=0)' beyond the dropouts), i.e. a completer/complete-case analysis, not ITT with imputation. Outlier/sensitivity handling ('sensitivity analyses of influential data points and priors') is mentioned but not detailed in the main text; full detail is deferred to Supplementary File S3 (WAMBS checklist), which was not extracted here (out of scope: task instructs extraction from paper.pdf).
